rationale: Image-processing evaluation of visual plant-disease signs on celery leaves, not human vision or consumption.
Existing Khalid case: oral celery root extract with venlafaxine and St Johns wort followed by mania; primary abstract does not specify hallucination type.
2018 systematic review describes the same Khalid root-drug case and explicitly warns against assuming causation; not a new case or dried leaf.
Ethanolic celery leaf extract studied in cultured cells and enzyme assays; no human visual hallucination.
Celery leaf and stem extracts studied in cultured inflammatory cells, not a human visual outcome.
Existing original dried-celery-leaf powder thyroid case; no visual hallucination measurement and simultaneous medical treatment limits dechallenge inference.
Celery leaf and acetaminophen toxicity studied in fish liver; no human visual symptoms.
Celery plants in a soil cadmium/mycorrhiza experiment; not human ingestion or perception.
